dashboard.title: About the Overview section
dashboard.lead: The overview screen shows read-only platform metrics (users, tests, sessions, open GDPR requests) and the latest activity from the audit log. Nothing is configured here — the dashboard is read-only.

what_you_configure.heading: What you see here
items: Aggregated platform metrics (account, test and active session counts)
Open data subject requests (DSR) and open DPA requests
Latest events from the audit log across every section

time_impact.heading: Timing
items: Metrics load when the page opens; fresh data appears after a refresh
Audit activity surfaces within seconds of a successful operation elsewhere in the admin
There is no auto-refresh — use a browser reload for live monitoring

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: The delta values on the cards are still static (a UI placeholder, not a real trend)
For product setting changes, go to the Settings or Security sections

tests.title: About the Tests section
tests.lead: This is where you manage every test on the platform — create, edit, archive and delete them. Filters by status, difficulty and category help you find a specific test in a large library.

what_you_configure.heading: What you configure
items: List filters: status (draft/published/archived), difficulty, branch (vertical)
Search by test title
Bulk-delete the selected tests
The test detail opens by clicking a row (edits happen in a separate editor)

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: Delete (single and bulk): immediate — the list updates optimistically
Bulk delete runs mutations sequentially — large selections may take a moment
Published tests appear in the live app within 5–60 minutes (React Query cache)

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: The "Owner" filter is currently a UI stub — it does not actually filter
A test can belong to multiple branches at once (the "branch" filter matches a substring)
Deleting a test also deletes every respondent answer — the operation cannot be undone

quick_test.title: About the Quick test section
quick_test.lead: You configure the quick-test template shown on the landing page. It is the first contact a new visitor has with the platform — a short, motivating test for a chosen audience.

what_you_configure.heading: What you configure
items: Quick-test visibility (shown / hidden on the site)
Test name and description (copy)
Vertical (General / Senior / Youth / Company)
Time in seconds, pass percentage, difficulty
List of included questions (editing happens in the Questions section)

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: Input change: optimistic cache update — the UI shows the new value immediately
Save: the server mutation runs in the background; the change is live within 5–60 minutes
No "revert" button — the cache updates even if the server fails

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: You only view questions here, you don't edit them — go to the Questions section for edits
The "vertical" stage influences scoring branching in the live app
The cache may hold the old configuration for up to 60 minutes — use a force refresh to verify immediately

share_card.title: About the Share card section
share_card.lead: You configure the Open Graph card used to share test results on social networks. The card shows up on Facebook, LinkedIn, WhatsApp and elsewhere when a user shares a link to a test or to their result.

what_you_configure.heading: What you configure
items: OG image URL (1200×630 px, max 5 MB, JPG/PNG)
Fallback title (required — used when a test has none of its own)
Fallback description (optional — a short motivating sentence)

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: The editor preview updates as you type (live preview)
The social-network cache (FB, LinkedIn) holds the old card — after a change you need to re-scrape via their developer tools
The configuration reaches the live app within 5–60 minutes

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: The title is validated as non-empty — saving without it fails with a toast
The image preview loads an external URL; a broken or 404 address shows up as an empty box
The Facebook / LinkedIn cache has to be invalidated manually via their "debugger" tools

questions.title: About the Questions section
questions.lead: The central library of every question on the platform. You create, edit, publish and archive them in bulk; you'll find both community-authored and editorial questions here. CSV export, filtering and pagination are supported.

what_you_configure.heading: What you configure
items: Question creation and editing (a modal with text, answers, explanation, category)
Bulk status change (publish / archive the selected items)
Bulk deletion
Filters: status, branch, author, vote count (-50 to +200), reported only
Export the filtered list to CSV (client-side, no server call)

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: Create / edit / delete: immediate server mutation + cache invalidation
Bulk operations run sequentially (not in parallel) — expect longer waits for 100+ records
The AI generator is toggled via the build-time variable VITE_AI_GENERATOR_ENABLED — a toggle requires a redeploy

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: Changing a filter always resets pagination to page 1
Authors without a name set (seeded questions) do not appear in the author dropdown
Negative votes start at -50 — there is no filter for lower scores

answer_sets.title: About the Answer sets section
answer_sets.lead: You manage reusable answer sets — groups of correct and incorrect options that get attached to questions. A set exists once and is used N times across questions; a change to the set is reflected in every question that uses it.

what_you_configure.heading: What you configure
items: Create a new set (opens the editor)
Duplicate a set (creates a new copy including every answer)
Delete a set
Search by set name
Set detail (edit answer text, ordering and correctness flag)

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: Set creation: immediate mutation + redirect to detail
Duplication: creates a new set + sequentially copies each answer (N+1 mutations, no rollback)
Deletion: immediate, optimistic removal from cache
The usage count on the card is stale until the query refetches

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: Duplication is not transactional — if it fails midway you end up with a new set with incomplete answers
Deleting a set used by a question can break that question's scoring (set → question link)
The correct/incorrect totals are computed at render time — for large sets they can be temporarily stale

links.label: Answer sets and the link to questions
Best practices for duplication and versioning

trainings.title: About the Trainings section
trainings.lead: You manage educational trainings — short courses the platform offers after a completed test or as a standalone. For each training you set the topic, length, publish status and descriptive content.

what_you_configure.heading: What you configure
items: Create a new training (modal editor)
Edit an existing one (name, topic, description, length, status)
Duplicate (a copy with the "(copy)" suffix and status forced to draft)
Delete
Search by name

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: Create / edit / delete: immediate server mutation + list invalidation
A published training appears in the live app within 5–60 minutes (React Query cache)
A duplicate always starts as a draft — publish it manually after review

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: The topic is picked from a fixed list — adding a new topic requires a DB migration
Length is informational (shown to the visitor) — it does not affect technical timeouts
Duplication also copies the description including any Markdown formatting

users.title: About the Users section
users.lead: A list of every registered account with its role and status. You see who is an admin, a user or pending confirmation; you filter by role, search by name or email, and see each user's question count.

what_you_configure.heading: What you configure
items: Search by display_name or email (client-side filter)
Filter by role: admin / user / pending
"Edit role" button — wired up in the UI, but the server mutation is not yet connected

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: Search and filter: purely client-side, no network overhead
Role change (once wired): immediate — applies from the affected user's next API call
Demotion from admin → user revokes access to /admin and signs the user out on their next click

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: The "Edit role" button is currently a UI stub — it shows a toast but does not change the DB
The role filter only knows admin / user / pending — custom roles do not show up
Avatar initials use the first 2 characters of display_name — they are empty when the name is empty

categories.title: About the Categories section
categories.lead: A two-level content taxonomy: branches (top-level) and topics (children of branches). A topic's slug starts with the branch slug (a convention, not an FK), which is why deleting a branch with children is blocked. Questions, tests and articles are tagged with these values.

what_you_configure.heading: What you configure
items: Branches: create, edit name/slug/description, delete (guarded when children exist)
Topics: create under a chosen branch, edit, delete
The slug auto-generates from the name (lowercase, dashes), but is editable

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: Create / edit / delete: immediate mutation + invalidation of both queries (branches + topics)
Attempting to delete a branch that has topics → the guard fails with an error toast
A slug change is propagated to the question link the next time those questions are saved (lazy migration)

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: The delete guard checks the naming convention, not an FK — a manual breach of the convention bypasses it
The colour is hardcoded to #6366f1 (indigo) — there is no colour picker yet
Re-parenting a topic into a different branch is not supported; create a new one and delete the old

reports.title: About the Reports section
reports.lead: Governance queue: users report questions here that violate the rules (spam, inappropriate content, harassment, misinformation). The admin reviews each report — either resolves it (taking action on the question) or dismisses it as unfounded.

what_you_configure.heading: What you configure
items: Filter by status (open / in progress / resolved / dismissed) and reason
Actions: resolve, dismiss (mutation + invalidation)
Export the filtered list to CSV

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: Filters: immediate (client-side on the loaded list)
Resolve / dismiss: immediate mutation + toast, the query is invalidated
Export: purely client-side — no server call, no size limit

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: Reasons and statuses are fixed enums — adding a new reason requires a code change
No manual priority or reordering — the queue is always sorted by created_at
Resolving a report does not delete the question — you have to do that separately in the Questions section

links.label: Escalation: when to delete a question vs. an author

support.title: About the Support section
support.lead: You configure the support channel contact details — email, phone and opening hours. These values are shown to visitors in the footer, on the contact page and in automated replies.

what_you_configure.heading: What you configure
items: Support email (required, regex-validated)
Phone number (optional, validated when filled in)
Opening hours (free text, e.g. "Mon–Fri 9:00–17:00")

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: Input: synchronous form state update
Save: validation + config write + success toast
The live app picks up the new configuration on its next init (short bootstrap delay)

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: Validation is client-side only (regex) — the server accepts any value you send
Hours have no format validation — typos reach the live app
This is currently an in-memory config scoped to the session; DB persistence is coming in the next iteration

blog.title: About the Blog section
blog.lead: You manage blog posts — drafts, published and archived. You create new posts, open the editor for existing ones and delete stale entries. The detailed editor (copy, images, SEO) opens by clicking a row.

what_you_configure.heading: What you configure
items: Create a new post (redirects to /admin/blog/new)
Edit an existing one (link to /admin/blog/$id)
Delete a post (inline action, mutation)
Post status is set in the detail editor (draft / published / archive)

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: Create: server mutation when the editor opens
Delete: immediate mutation + list refetch
A published post is available on the site immediately; build-time RSS and sitemap are generated at deploy time

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: No bulk operations — deletion is one row at a time
A post slug is required and unique; a slug error fails the save
A published post only reaches sitemap.xml on the next deploy (npm run build)

pages.title: About the Pages section
pages.lead: You manage the static CMS pages of the site — terms, contact, privacy policy and similar. The detail editor works with blocks (heading, text, image…) that you assemble into the final page.

what_you_configure.heading: What you configure
items: Create a new page (after creation, redirect to detail)
Edit a page (name, slug, status, blocks)
Publish / unpublish (toggle in the detail editor)
Delete a page
Page blocks: add, delete, move up/down (ChevronUp/Down)

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: Block input: optimistic cache update + async mutation
Publish: optimistic published_at + mutation + invalidation
The live app will see the page within 5–60 minutes (React Query cache)

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: The slug must match /^[a-z0-9-]+$/ — diacritics, spaces and uppercase letters are rejected
Block reordering is swap-by-index (not drag & drop) — it gets inefficient at 20+ blocks
The detail editor reads from the listing query — if the page isn't cached, it shows "not found"

navigation.title: About the Navigation section
navigation.lead: You configure the site's main menu — items, their order, visibility to signed-in users and opening in a new tab. This menu shows up in the header on both desktop and mobile.

what_you_configure.heading: What you configure
items: Add an item (auto-ID, empty label/url, position = count + 1)
Edit in a dialog: label, URL, open_in_new_tab, auth_only
Delete an item
Move up / down (swap positions with the neighbour)
Inline toggle for visibility and "signed-in only"

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: Every change: optimistic cache update + async mutation
Delete + move: query invalidation after success
The live app will see the menu within 5–60 minutes (React Query cache)

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: URLs must match /^(\/[^\s]*|https:\/\/[^\s]+)$/ — only local paths or https:// are accepted
Position is numeric — skipping (1, 2, 5) leaves a gap; swap-by-index ignores it
auth_only is just a UI flag — the back-end does not enforce it, a user sees the item if they know the URL

header.title: About the Header section
header.lead: You configure the site's global header — logo, primary CTA button and the mobile menu label. Visitors see these values in the top bar on every public page.

what_you_configure.heading: What you configure
items: logo_url — URL of the logo image
cta_label — text of the primary button (e.g. "Start test")
cta_url — where the button points to
mobile_trigger_label — text of the mobile menu trigger (a11y label)

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: Input: optimistic cache update + async mutation
Save: success toast (no further action)
The live app will see the new header within 5–60 minutes (React Query cache)

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: Logo URL is just a string — a 404 or wrong format shows up as an empty image
cta_url has no URL validation — an invalid value redirects to 404
The form does not lock the fields while saving — fast clicks can spam mutations

footer.title: About the Footer section
footer.lead: You manage the site footer — columns of links and social networks. Visitors see the footer on every public page; it also serves SEO interlinking and the mandatory GDPR/cookie links.

what_you_configure.heading: What you configure
items: Columns: add, edit name, delete
Links in a column: add, edit label/url, delete
Social networks: add a platform + URL, edit, delete
Column order is determined by creation order (drag-reorder is not yet available)

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: Every change: optimistic cache update + async mutation
The live app will see the new footer within 5–60 minutes (React Query cache)
Social icons render based on the platform string — an unknown platform → generic icon

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: Link URLs / social URLs have no validation — invalid values can slip through
To change column order you have to delete and recreate (no drag & drop)
The social-network platform is free text — a typo like "Insagram" will miss the known icons

links.label: GDPR / cookie links in the footer (mandatory)

dsr.title: About the GDPR requests section
dsr.lead: Governance queue for data subject requests under GDPR (art. 15–22) — access, rectification, erasure, portability. Each request has an SLA based on its type and status; coloured badges call out an upcoming deadline.

what_you_configure.heading: What you configure
items: Filter by status (open / in progress / resolved / dismissed) and type (access / erasure / portability)
Search by requester email or note
Actions: resolve (status → completed) or dismiss (status → rejected)
Export the filtered list to CSV

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: Status mutation: immediate + query invalidation + toast
The SLA is computed client-side from created_at + a type-specific deadline (art. 12(3) = 30 days)
The "Overdue" badge fires when the deadline is crossed
Mutations run one at a time — if one fails midway the UI is temporarily inconsistent

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: GDPR art. 12(3) sets 1 month to resolve — overdue is a legal breach
Resolving does not cover the technical execution of the request (e.g. the actual erasure) — you do that outside this queue
Search is free text without AND/OR operators — it covers the email and a substring of the note

links.label: Technical runbook for erasure and anonymisation

dpa_requests.title: About the DPA requests section
dpa_requests.lead: Governance queue for Data Processing Agreement / NDA requests. You track the request lifecycle (pending / received / signed / cancelled) and the status of the dispatched email. PDF download, re-send and anonymisation are available per row.

what_you_configure.heading: What you configure
items: Filter by request status and email status, search by requester email
Change status (dropdown or button)
Anonymise (one-way: PII → ****, status → cancelled)
Re-send the email (re-trigger SMTP send)
Download the signed PDF
Export to CSV

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: Status change: immediate mutation + invalidation
Anonymisation: IRREVERSIBLE — PII is overwritten, status is forced to cancelled
Re-send: async SMTP job — email_status flips from "pending" to "sent"/"failed" only after it finishes
PDF download: server call, the browser downloads the file

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: Anonymisation is a one-way operation — verify the requester's identity carefully before clicking
Request status and email status are separate — you can have a "pending" request with a "sent" email
The dashboard counts open requests by request status only, not by email status

settings.title: About the Settings section
settings.lead: Read-only GDPR / compliance dashboard. It shows the current values of feature flags (DPA flow on/off, draft watermark, DPA template version) and the retention policy. Changes are made via env variables in Cloudflare Pages — that requires a redeploy and leaves an audit trail in the deploy log.

what_you_configure.heading: What you see here (read-only)
items: DPA flow: VITE_DPA_FLOW_ENABLED (true/false)
Draft watermark: VITE_DPA_TEMPLATE_DRAFT_WATERMARK
DPA template version: hardcoded in src/lib/dpa/feature-flag.ts
Retention policy: SQL function anonymize_expired_dpa_requests() — runs on cron
List of subprocessors (hardcoded SUB_PROCESSORS constant)

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: Env flag change: edit in the Cloudflare Pages dashboard + redeploy (about 3–5 minutes)
DPA template version change: code change + PR + merge + redeploy
Retention cron: runs per the cron expression in Supabase (default once a day)
Subprocessor update: code change (legally sensitive — requires legal team review)

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: The page is read-only on purpose — env-backed flags must leave a deploy audit trail
No live toggle: a change without a redeploy has no effect
The watermark renders in amber when ON (warning against production use) and green when OFF

security.title: About the Security section
security.lead: Self-service MFA for your own admin account — TOTP authenticator (Google Authenticator, 1Password, …) and backup codes. There are no global settings here; this section only manages factors for the currently signed-in admin.

what_you_configure.heading: What you configure
items: Enroll 2FA (redirects to /login/enroll-2fa)
Reset 2FA (unenroll the factor, confirm, redirect to re-enroll)
Generate new backup codes (confirm, shown in a modal with copy/download)
Show the count of remaining backup codes

time_impact.heading: Timing of changes
items: Enroll: redirect into the flow; after completion the factor appears immediately on refresh
Unenroll: immediate mutation, redirect to re-enroll (you have to enroll again!)
Code regeneration: mutation + modal (the server saves immediately)
Backup codes < 3 → warning (hardcoded threshold)

pitfalls.heading: Watch out for
items: Reset 2FA redirects to re-enroll immediately — you have to enroll the authenticator again
Backup codes are not stored locally anywhere; closing the modal without saving = codes lost (the server has them, you don't)
The system does not block unenrolling the last factor — the next sign-in will not be protected by 2FA
